evidence.title: Meter quality checks (ALL)
evidence.sql:
WITH base AS (SELECT site_id, ts, kwh FROM kilowhy.meter_hh WHERE site_id IN ('S1', 'S2', 'S3') AND ts >= timestamp '2026-08-27 00:00:00' AND ts < timestamp '2026-10-22 00:00:00'),
lagged AS (SELECT site_id, ts, kwh, LAG(kwh) OVER (PARTITION BY site_id ORDER BY ts) AS prev_kwh FROM base),
grp AS (SELECT site_id, ts, kwh, SUM(CASE WHEN prev_kwh IS NULL OR kwh <> prev_kwh THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY site_id ORDER BY ts) AS g FROM lagged),
runs AS (SELECT site_id, kwh, g, MIN(ts) AS start_ts, MAX(ts) AS end_ts, COUNT(*) AS n FROM grp GROUP BY site_id, kwh, g)
SELECT CASE WHEN kwh = 0 THEN 'zero_run' ELSE 'flatline' END AS check_name, site_id, CAST(start_ts AS STRING) AS start_ts, CAST(end_ts AS STRING) AS end_ts, n, kwh AS value FROM runs WHERE (kwh = 0 AND n >= 4) OR (kwh <> 0 AND n >= 12)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'duplicate_ts', site_id, CAST(ts AS STRING), CAST(ts AS STRING), COUNT(*), CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) FROM base GROUP BY site_id, ts HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
UNION ALL
SELECT 'slots_per_day', site_id, CAST(CAST(ts AS DATE) AS STRING), CAST(CAST(ts AS DATE) AS STRING), COUNT(*), CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) FROM base GROUP BY site_id, CAST(ts AS DATE) HAVING COUNT(*) <> 48
UNION ALL
SELECT 'rows', site_id, CAST(MIN(ts) AS STRING), CAST(MAX(ts) AS STRING), COUNT(*), SUM(kwh) FROM base GROUP BY site_id
ORDER BY check_name, site_id, start_ts

SELECT m.site_id, CASE WHEN m.ts >= timestamp '2026-08-27 00:00:00' AND m.ts < timestamp '2026-09-24 00:00:00' THEN 'A' ELSE 'B' END AS win, COUNT(*) AS n_slots, SUM(m.kwh) AS kwh, SUM(m.kwh * r.p_kwh_inc_vat) AS agile_inc_pence, SUM(m.kwh * f.p_kwh_exc_vat) AS flat_exc_pence, SUM(f.standing_p_day_exc_vat) / 48.0 AS flat_standing_exc_pence, MIN(f.p_kwh_exc_vat) AS flat_rate_min_exc, MAX(f.p_kwh_exc_vat) AS flat_rate_max_exc

answer.headline: Bill rose by £339.91 (17.0%) driven by higher prices and cold weather

sentences.text: The electricity bill increased by £339.91 (17.0%) compared to the previous four weeks, mainly because higher wholesale prices added £186.66.
Colder weather pushed up usage, adding £127.71 through the weather-driven volume effect.
A shift toward more gas generation (up 4.2 pp) also raised half-hourly prices.
A single day accounted for 30.9% of the total bill increase.
An unusual usage day at one site used 124 kWh due to a freezer fault.

ruledOut.text: Timing shifts were negligible (peak-band share changed by 0.2 pp, largest daily move below threshold).
No meter faults were found across 3 sites.
Standing charge stayed at 37.65 p/day per day.
No missing or extra half-hours in 6 site-windows.

recommendation.text: Shifting up to 10.0 kWh of flexible load per site per day out of the 16:00-19:00 peak band into cheaper periods (10:00-13:00, 04:00-07:00, 21:00-24:00) could save around £5.23 and cut carbon by 1.0 kgCO2e based on window B prices; a flat tariff would have cost £504.69 more in window B and £510.52 more in window A as a historical counterfactual.
